title: Polynomial threshold functions determined by low-degree coefficients
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f,g:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$. Suppose there is a real-valued function $p$ on the cube such that $f(x)$ is the sign of $p(x)$ at every input, taking sign $1$ when $p(x)\\ge 0$, and the Fourier degree of $p$ is at most $k$. If the real-valued versions of $f$ and $g$ have equal Fourier coefficients on every set of coordinates of size at most $k$, then $g=f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is represented by the threshold sign of a real-valued function $p$
The Fourier degree of $p$ is at most $k$
Their real-valued versions have equal Fourier coefficients for every coordinate set of size at most $k$
